item.title: The Story of VS Code — Fri Sep 4, 11:00 AM
item.description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto ​Erich Gamma once called VS Code an overnight success 10 years in the making.
​Those 10 years were pretty eventful. Before becoming one of the most widely used developer tools in the world, VS Code started with a small team building online developer tools out of Zurich, called itself Monaco, then Visual Studio Online Monaco, then Ticino (because why not?), became a desktop editor, went open source, became an ecosystem in its own right, went back to the browser, and helped establish a whole bunch of open protocols along the way.
​And just when it felt like the hard part was done, AI happened.
​This is the story of how VS Code got here, told by the people who built it and the developers who helped shape it. And now, how it’s adapting once again as AI changes what a code editor can be.

item.title: La Société d'histoire de Toronto: HISTORITOUR - L’auberge Montgomery — Sat Sep 5, 1:30 PM — Montgomery’s Inn
item.description:
Départ : Devant l’auberge Montgomery sur la pelouse, coin sud-est de l’avenue Islington et de la rue Dundas ouest (TTC ligne 2 jusqu’à Islington, bus 37 jusqu’à la rue Dundas) Parking disponible à l’auberge. Arrivée : même lieu Guide: Marie-Claude Douville L’Auberge Montgomery a été construite par la famille du même nom dans les années 1830. Ce musée de la ville de Toronto représente bien la vie au 19e siècle avec des chambres à coucher, une salle à manger, des pièces privées, une taverne et une salle communautaire. La cuisine est toujours fonctionnelle et le four à pain à l’extérieur cuit chaque semaine pour le marché du mercredi. Historitours 2026 – pas nécessaire de réserver. La SHT passe le chapeau à la fin de la visite, merci. Pas de chien Contacts : mcdouville@yahoo.ca ou info@sht.ca

item.title: Hamilton Public Library Lecture: Stonehenge of the Americas — Wed Sep 9, 6:00 PM — Hamilton Public Library – Central Library
item.description:
HPL Lecture Series: Stonehenge of the Americas? The Rise and Fall of Tiwanaku
High in the Bolivian Andes, on the shores of Lake Titicaca, lies Tiwanaku — often called the Stonehenge of the Americas. Around the end of the fourth century AD, this remarkable settlement underwent a dramatic transformation, becoming the first city in the highlands of Andean South America. What triggered this sudden explosion of political power, economic innovation and artistic creativity?
Drawing on 25 years of archaeological research, this talk explores discoveries that are reshaping our understanding of Tiwanaku’s origins, the environmental and social forces behind its rise and the factors that ultimately led to its decline.
Central Library (55 York Blvd.) – Hamilton Room Wednesday, September 9 – 6-8pm (talk starts 6:30pm) REGISTRATION LINK
Source: Ontario Historical Society

item.description:
Guest Speaker: Catherine Willis-O’Connor, Artist Details Artist Catherine Willis-O’Connor began contemplating how the arrival of the Ottawa’s LRT would soon impact neighbourhood culture, and so she set out to capture the memories of the businesses, houses, parks and streetscapes that have come to define our city’s ambiance. Catherine has always felt a connection with history. She is the grand-daughter of WWI flying ace Billy Bishop, great-great-granddaugher of department store founder Timothy Eaton, and great-great-granddaugher of Daniel O’Connor, one of Bytown’s most prominent citizens. Join Catherine as she animates Ottawa’s past by guiding us through her joyous paintings, each of which promises to unleash a treasure trove of memories. This presentation will take place on Zoom. All are welcome. Zoom registration: tinyurl.com/HSO-9-Sep-2026

item.description:

Discover the fascinating qualities of silverpoint, a drawing medium favoured during the Middle Ages and Renaissance by old masters, such as Leonardo Da Vinci and Albrecht Dürer. Participants will create an original silverpoint drawing of a leaf onto a prepared board that will develop warm brown tones as it ages. Beginners welcome.
Each attendee will receive a silver drawing pencil and learn how to continue using this medium beyond the classroom.

Départ : Rencontre au coin sud-est des rues Jarvis et Carlton – le tram 506 vous y dépose Fin : Dans le parc Guides : Béatrice Luneau et Rolande Smith Terrain plat Depuis sa création en 1858, le parc Allan Gardens n’a cessé de voir la ville grandir autour de lui. L’ensemble de ses six serres ont été installées au fur et à mesure des années (The Palm House en 1910, The Temperate House en 1924 et les autres dans les années 50). Certaines serres ont été transférées de l’Exhibition Place et de l’Université de Toronto. Venez découvrir ce que cet ensemble vous offre aujourd’hui. Cette visite se fera en plusieurs étapes commençant par une présentation en salle sur l’histoire du parc et des serres, puis une visite des serres et si le temps le permet un tour du parc et de ses arbres. Pas nécessaire de réserver. La Société d’histoire de Toronto passe le chapeau à la fin de la visite. Pas de chien. Contacts : info@sht.ca ou smth7631@rogers.com
Source: Ontario Historical Society

item.title: Birding with Beni: Fall Birding — Fri Sep 18, 8:00 AM — Toronto Botanical Garden
item.description:
Join us for a fall birding nature walk! Fall migration is well underway! Join TBG Horticulturist and avid birder Sasan Beni for an engaging walk through the gardens and Wilket Creek Ravine, as you seek out the wildlife that call this place home. Learn how to identify the many different species passing through and how you can help them in their journey.
Bring your binoculars for a better view (we will have extras on hand) and a mug/thermos for a warm beverage and post-birding chat.
As with any wildlife tour, the spotting of birds and other wildlife is not guaranteed and is not within the control of the tour guide. Please be patient and considerate. The tour will not be rescheduled due to a lack of bird sightings. The tour will only be rescheduled due to inclement weather.
Meet at the TBG main entrance, just outside the George and Kathy Dembroski Centre for Horticulture.
Friday, September 18, 8 to 10 a.m. Public $22, Members $20 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
